driver: A per-record date is constructed from an event log with a class-conditional cut, because a filed clause bars one record class from a late capacity slot that began after the closed validation window, so the classless construction reproduces the corpus exactly yet overstates a per-period threshold hinge until that class's late records roll forward a period.
driver_concrete: Clause 2.3 reserves the evening Rawtenstall hub trunk (17 Rushden departures from 26 April 2028) to Guaranteed Services, so N48 and BKY consignments manifested after the last Kettering depot pull are accepted the next operating day; 5,101 consignments move off surcharged days and the surcharge falls from GBP 18,986.21 to GBP 16,078.88.
stump: A competent solver builds acceptance dates from the yard log against manifest timestamps, validates them 29 of 29 against the carrier's April daily statement, receipts and invoice, and files GBP 18,986.21, because no trunk ran in April so the classless and per-service cuts are identical there.
